opportunities.claim: For a primitive finite-dimensional KMS-symmetric QMS, the weak p=1 endpoint J >= 2E implies the complete weak Lp-regularity family for every finite p >= 1.
opportunities.primary_mechanism: Kastoryano-Temme Lemma 18: convexity of h(s) for every s in [0,2] and all positive g,t implies weak Lp for all finite p, with p=2/(2-s).
opportunities.exact_missing_step: Derive the full h(s)-convexity/secant family or a separate interpolation theorem from only the p=1 endpoint; no checked source states this implication.
opportunities.scope: KT Definition 9 requires the inequalities for all p. Lemma 18's all-interval convexity is sufficient, not necessary. No implication or counterexample established here.

opportunities.claim: For arbitrary faithful finite-dimensional KMS-symmetric dynamics, compare the entropy-resolvent dissipation with the square-root KMS Dirichlet energy with a dimension-independent constant; target candidate is J >= 2E.
opportunities.primary_mechanism: VW arXiv:2303.15949v2 Theorems 2.4-2.5 give a KMS-twisted derivation and exact commutator Dirichlet form; VW arXiv:2610.09678v1 Theorems 3.9 and 4.4 give accretive modular action and a modular-orbit commutator representation. The latter is prior art for the parent-supplied finite orbit formula after t=-2u and tracking the factor 1/2.
opportunities.exact_missing_step: Prove an integrated/pointwise comparison between the parent-supplied entropy-resolvent Gamma_L terms and the known VW modular-orbit form, or prove the supplied root superoperator M is positive for all faithful sigma,rho. No checked source gives either comparison.
compatibility_obligations: Keep Schrödinger state evolution and Heisenberg KMS generator adjoints/conjugations explicit.
Do not import Carlen-Maas logarithmic chain rule outside its GNS/modular-covariant assumptions.
Do not replace the KMS twist by a conventional Hilbert-bimodule derivation; Vernooij Example 5.3 blocks that route for a concrete KMS form.

opportunities.claim: For the supplied finite-dimensional KMS target, the stationary entropy-production Hessian satisfies J2 >= pi E2, where the physical tangent Z is converted to square-root tangent Y by Z=sY+Ys and E2=<Y,H Y>_HS.
opportunities.primary_mechanism: Gao-Guo arXiv:2609.15902v1 Theorem 1.1 and Definition 2.10 compare BKM coercivity with MLSI. Example 6.4 gives a genuine KMS obstruction to positive BKM coercivity, but its Hessian denominator is the BKM metric, not the target square-root Dirichlet energy.
opportunities.exact_missing_step: Compare the BKM second-variation numerator on a physical tangent Z with the HS Dirichlet form on Y=(L_s+R_s)^(-1)Z, preserving Schrödinger/Heisenberg signs and normalization. The source BKM-zero family has not been shown to violate the target after this conversion.
opportunities.scope: A finite numerical map of Gao-Guo's Example 6.4 gives J2/E2 above pi at sampled eps values only; it is not a proof or an asymptotic claim. No theorem or exact counterexample matching J2/E2 was found in this bounded check. No novelty claim follows from absence.
